surprise.title: The clouds clear out at 3, and golden hour runs 5:08 to 5:58 tonight
surprise.body: Today starts under a solid gray lid, fully overcast through 2 PM, but the forecast shows the sky clearing almost completely by 3 PM and staying clear into the evening, with no rain anywhere in the day. That makes tonight the first clean golden hour in a while: the warm, low light starts around 5:08 PM, the sun sets at 5:42 PM a little south of due west (about 250° on a compass), and the soft blue hour follows from about 5:58 to 6:07 PM, with civil twilight ending at 6:07. It will be in the mid 70s when the light turns gold and cooling toward 67°F by 6. If you want fresh Grad Arena portfolio frames, put your subject facing west-southwest around 5:15 for glowing skin and long shadows, then flip to backlit silhouettes in the last ten minutes before sunset. And if you would rather just enjoy it, the North Florida Fair opens its gates at 5 PM, so the midway lights come on right as the sky goes orange.

source.label: Sunset and twilight from sunrise-sunset.org; golden and blue hour computed for Tallahassee (sun 6° to -4°); cloud cover and temperature from Open-Meteo
